injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

source: The Plaintiff was found to be suffering from open dislocation of right knee and there was no circulation of right leg nor sensation/movement of right leg/ankle/foot.

Emergency operation was performed and intra-operative findings included (1) popliteal artery rupture; (2) stretched posterior tibial nerve and peroneal nerve; (3) rupture both heads of gastrocnemius; (4) gross laxity right keen (anterior and posterior cruciate ligament rupture).

source: Neurologists assessment revealed that the Plaintiff was likely suffering from common peroneal nerve palsy.
A nerve conduction test was done on 28 May 2004. The results shown unelicitable right peroneal motor potential. The right sural nerve potential was also absent.
Electromyelogram of right peroneal shown fibrillation, fasciculation and polyphasia. The clinical impression was only limited recovery of right peroneal nerve.

source: There were multiple scars over both limbs including a 15 cm oblique scar over the back of the right lower thigh; a patch of skin graft donor site rectangular scar measuring 10 x 5 cm; and a 9 cm long scar over the medial site of the left ankle where the vein graft was harvested (photographs depicting the scars can be found at pp 455 to 461 of the hearing bundle).

manifestations.description: Right knee joint laxity (feeling experienced during all motions and activities including walking on level ground)
Right knee pain provoked by walking more than an hour; no pain at rest
Right knee soreness over the front of the knee when walking on stairs
Right knee stiffness after sitting for more than 30 to 45 minutes
Right foot drop condition with tendency to trip over when she walked; must lift right foot clear of the floor when she walked
Decreased sensation over the back and lateral side of the right leg
Feeling of right calf swollen up after walking for an hour
Pain on pressing the left ankle medial side scar (vein graft donor site)
Lumbar back pain, more on the right side, worse when she walked
Left heel pain after walking for an hour
Walked with right drop foot mild limping gait; not able to walk on heels and not able to squat down
Limitation in range of motion: knee (0° to 120° right; 0° to 145° left); ankle dorsiflexion (0° right; 15° left); ankle plantar flexion (30° right; 40° left)

Reduced muscle power at the limb joint (hip flexion 4+ right, 5 left; hip extension 4+ right, 5 left; knee flexion 4- right, 5 left; knee extension 4- right, 5 left; ankle dorsiflexion 1 right, 5 left; ankle plantar flexion 5- right, 5 left; big toe flexion 4 right, 5 left; big toe extension 4- right, 5 left)
Visible scarring over lower limbs (including described scars)

treatments_received: emergency operation with application of external fixation
saphenous vein graft to popliteal artery
removal of external fixator and change to a long leg hinge brace
manipulation of right knee to improve range of movement
split skin graft of right popliteal fossa
arthroscopy and shaving of medial meniscus
treatments_future: posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction surgery (to be done in December 2008)
tendon transfer operation (to be done after posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction)

losses.description: Residual impairment of right lower limb and knee including ruptured anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments, torn medial meniscus, open dislocation of right knee and associated functional limitations, pain and instability.

Reduced walking endurance, painful and exhausting walking on level ground, need for walking stick and soft brace for right knee, inability to walk on heels, mild limping gait and tendency to trip due to right foot drop.

Multiple scars over both lower limbs including a 15 cm oblique scar over the back of the right lower thigh, skin graft donor site rectangular scar 10 x 5 cm and a 9 cm long scar over the medial site of the left ankle.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to perform heavy household chores such as mopping, climbing on chair or table to reach high shelves or windows; entitled to part time helper for light chores.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Previously enjoyed hiking, bowling, traveling, shopping, touring by motorcycle and playing badminton; now very inconvenient to resume such activities.
